categories.main_business_segments: VeriSilicon Microelectronics (Shanghai) Co., Ltd. primarily operates in two main business segments: semiconductor IP licensing and one-stop chip customization services. The IP licensing includes GPU, NPU, VPU, DSP, ISP, and display processing IPs, while the chip customization services cover chip design and mass production services. The company also provides software development platforms and system-level solutions for various applications.
categories.core_technologies_production_methods: The company leverages proprietary semiconductor IP technologies including advanced GPU, NPU, VPU, DSP, ISP, and display processing IPs, along with over 1,600 analog/mixed-signal and RF IPs. It supports advanced semiconductor process nodes such as 5nm/7nm FinFET and 22nm FD-SOI. VeriSilicon employs a Silicon Platform as a Service (SiPaaS) model integrating IP cores, chip design, and software development. The company also focuses on Chiplet technology, advanced packaging (SiP, 2.5D CoWoS), and ISO 26262 certified automotive functional safety design flows.
categories.primary_customers_markets: Key customers include chip design companies, IDM, system manufacturers, large internet companies, cloud service providers, and automotive OEMs. Major end markets served are AI computing (AIGC), data centers, automotive electronics (including ADAS and autonomous driving), wearable devices (smartwatches, AR/VR glasses), IoT, consumer electronics, and industrial applications. The company has collaborations with global leaders such as Samsung, Google, Amazon, Microsoft, and leading Chinese internet firms.
categories.geographic_coverage: VeriSilicon operates globally with subsidiaries and offices in China (Shanghai, Beijing, Chengdu, Nanjing, Hainan), the United States (Silicon Valley, Dallas), Hong Kong, Japan, France, Vietnam, and the Cayman Islands. Revenue is generated both domestically (62.57%) and internationally (37.43%), with significant growth in overseas sales. The company maintains a global sales and technical support network covering China, Taiwan, the US, Europe, Japan, and South Korea.
categories.supply_chain_position: The company operates primarily in the upstream and midstream segments of the semiconductor supply chain, focusing on semiconductor IP development and chip design services. It outsources wafer manufacturing, packaging, and testing to specialized foundries and subcontractors, maintaining a fabless business model. VeriSilicon acts as a technology provider and design service partner rather than a chip manufacturer.
categories.strategic_focus_rd_direction: Strategic priorities include advancing Chiplet technology for AIGC and smart mobility applications, continuous enhancement of semiconductor IPs (GPU, NPU, VPU, etc.), and expanding system-level chip customization platforms. The company invests heavily in R&D, with over 53% of revenue allocated to research, focusing on AI acceleration, automotive functional safety, low-power IoT connectivity, and software ecosystems. It actively promotes RISC-V ecosystem development and collaborates on open-source AI security frameworks.
categories.revenue_model: Revenue is generated through licensing fees for semiconductor IP cores, royalties based on chip production volumes, and fees from one-stop chip customization services including design and mass production management. The company also earns income from software development platforms and related technical support services. The business model emphasizes upfront IP licensing fees, milestone payments during chip design, and ongoing royalties from volume production.
categories.key_competitors_industry_positioning: VeriSilicon is the leading semiconductor IP provider in China and ranks eighth globally by IP licensing revenue. It competes with international semiconductor IP and design service companies such as ARM, Cadence, and Synopsys. The company holds a strong position in AI-related IPs and chip design services, with a growing footprint in automotive, data center, and wearable markets. Its fabless and platform-based SiPaaS model differentiates it from traditional chip manufacturers and design houses.
categories.financial_scale_growth_profile: In 2024, VeriSilicon reported revenues of approximately RMB 2.32 billion, roughly flat compared to 2023. The company experienced a net loss attributable to shareholders of RMB 600.9 million, with increased R&D expenses accounting for over 53% of revenue. Total assets reached RMB 4.63 billion, with net assets of RMB 2.12 billion. The company maintains a strong order backlog exceeding RMB 2.4 billion and shows growth in overseas sales (+63.59%). It continues to invest heavily in R&D and talent, preparing for future growth in AI and automotive sectors.
categories.value_proposition_product_differentiatio: VeriSilicon offers a comprehensive, platform-based chip design and semiconductor IP service model (SiPaaS) that integrates proprietary, high-performance IP cores with flexible chip customization and software solutions. Its unique Chiplet technology and advanced packaging capabilities enable rapid, cost-effective development of complex AI and automotive chips. The company emphasizes low-power, high-efficiency designs certified for automotive safety standards and supports a broad ecosystem including RISC-V and open-source AI frameworks. This integrated approach reduces customer design risk, shortens time-to-market, and enhances product differentiation.
